- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after sentiment spikes.
- In periods of high volatility (sentiment swings >0.5), forecast mean reversion is stronger; dampen trend components by 15–25%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture downward momentum after 10–12 days; apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day after day 10.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.2–0.6), model tends to drift upward; apply a downward correction of 0.5–1.0% to avoid false momentum.
